- [X] ran `brew update` and can still reproduce the problem?

- [X] ran `brew doctor`, fixed all issues and can still reproduce the problem?

**[This](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/files/3545361/brew-doctor.txt) is what I got from `brew doctor`**

- [X] ran `brew gist-logs <formula>` (where `<formula>` is the name of the formula that failed) and included the output link?

**Yields this**:

```bash
10:20:09 [admin@brandizmac ~]$ brew gist-logs rclone
Error: No logs.

```

- [X] if `brew gist-logs` didn't work: ran `brew config` and `brew doctor` and included their output with your issue?

To help us debug your issue please explain:

- What you were trying to do (and why)

**I've installed rclone and everything works fine except...**

- What happened (include command output)

**...that, when I login as root (`su - root`) I get an error from the bash completion integration script**:

```bash
10:20:15 [brandizi@brandizmac ~]$ su - root
Password:
-sh: /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone: line 266: syntax error near unexpected token `<'
-sh: /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone: line 266: `            done < <(command rclone listremotes)'
10:20:18 [root@brandizmac ~]#
```

Note that this happens for the root user only. I tried to see if it is missing something from the PATH, or file permissions, but no luck.

- What you expected to happen

**No complaints and bash completion working for rclone (works for other users)**

- Step-by-step reproduction instructions (by running `brew install` commands)

  1. `sudo - root`

body:
Are you using the same version of bash as root as you are as a user?  Can you try this as root and a user?

```
$  echo "${BASH_VERSION}"
5.0.3(1)-release
```

That code comes from here BTW if we need to patch it.

https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/693112d57e0aaece5f6ec46100bedb818794dcef/cmd/help.go#L53

Cc: @sgtpep for a second opinion

Hi @ncw, I forgot to report this, but yes, it's the same bash:

```bash
13:14:44 [brandizi@brandizmac ~]$ which bash
/bin/bash
13:14:54 [brandizi@brandizmac ~]$ bash -version
GNU bash, version 3.2.57(1)-release (x86_64-apple-darwin18)
Copyright (C) 2007 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
13:14:58 [brandizi@brandizmac ~]$
13:15:25 [brandizi@brandizmac ~]$ su -
Password:
-sh: /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone: line 266: syntax error near unexpected token `<'
-sh: /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone: line 266: `            done < <(command rclone listremotes)'
13:15:30 [root@brandizmac ~]# which bash
/bin/bash
13:15:34 [root@brandizmac ~]# bash -version
GNU bash, version 3.2.57(1)-release (x86_64-apple-darwin18)
Copyright (C) 2007 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
13:15:39 [root@brandizmac ~]#
```

which is the one shipped with macOS.

The process substution syntax `<(command)` has been since bash 2 so bash 3 should be OK with that.

Does the autocomplete work as root or a user?

So if you type `rclone ls ` then press TAB twice do you get a list of all your remotes and all the local directories?

What happens if you `source /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone` as root and a user?

@ncw By chance I now have a macOS with the same exact version of bash. I tried `done < <(...)` construct on it and it didn't raise any error. It's weird, I have no other suggestions for diagnostics apart from `source /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone`.

@marco-brandizi Sorry to ask you, but could you also upload `/usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone` to something like GitHub Gist or Pastebin? In this case I'll be able to reproduce it on my macOS device which I wouldn't like to pollute with Homebrew at the moment.

I get this when I try to auto-complete rclone:

```bash
16:08:34 [brandizi@brandizmac luke]$ rclone ls -bash: compopt: command not found
rres-onedrive:-bash: compopt: command not found
```
and then it works correctly. It doesn't work at all under root.

The autocompletion file is [here][10] (I had to change its extension into .txt, but just because GH doesn't allow uploads otherwise).

[10]: https://github.com/rclone/rclone/files/3556229/rclone.txt

`source /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone` gives me the same error when under root, no error under regular user.

More funny things:
```bash
16:27:22 [brandizi@brandizmac ~]$ su -
Password:
-sh: /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone: line 266: syntax error near unexpected token `<'
-sh: /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone: line 266: `            done < <(command rclone listremotes)'
16:27:26 [root@brandizmac ~]# cat < <(echo bla blah)
-sh: syntax error near unexpected token `<'
16:27:27 [root@brandizmac ~]#
16:27:29 [root@brandizmac ~]# bash
16:27:34 [root@brandizmac ~]# cat < <(echo bla blah)
bla blah
16:27:35 [root@brandizmac ~]#
16:27:37 [root@brandizmac ~]# exit
16:27:40 [root@brandizmac ~]# logout
16:27:42 [brandizi@brandizmac ~]$ cat < <(echo bla blah)
bla blah
16:27:46 [brandizi@brandizmac ~]$
```

So, must be something with the environment that is initialised  for my root, but no idea what. Since it doesn't seem rclone-specific anymore, I guess you should close this issue (and maybe open a new one for the `compopt` thing).

> I get this when I try to auto-complete rclone:
> 
> ```shell
> 16:08:34 [brandizi@brandizmac luke]$ rclone ls -bash: compopt: command not found
> rres-onedrive:-bash: compopt: command not found
> ```

Thank you! @ncw Indeed, there's no `compopt` in macOS's native bash which is used twice in `__rclone_custom_func`. They should be used together with a check like `[[ $(type -t compopt) = "builtin" ]]` and fallback to macOS's alternative `complete -o ...` if possible.

Here's the patch to prevent `compopt` from calling on macOS:
```
--- /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone   2019-08-29 18:38:02.254440170 +0300
+++ /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone~   2019-08-29 18:37:55.735182170 +0300
@@ -280,9 +280,9 @@
                 local reply=${prefix:+$prefix/}$line
                 [[ $reply != $path* ]] || COMPREPLY+=("$reply")
             done < <(rclone lsf "${cur%%:*}:$prefix" 2>/dev/null)
-           [[ ! ${COMPREPLY[@]} ]] || compopt -o filenames
+           [[ ! ${COMPREPLY[@]} || $(type -t compopt) != builtin ]] || compopt -o filenames
         fi
-        [[ ! ${COMPREPLY[@]} ]] || compopt -o nospace
+        [[ ! ${COMPREPLY[@]} || $(type -t compopt) != builtin ]] || compopt -o nospace
     fi
 }
``` 

Also, to someone who wants to emulate `compopt` options on macOS there's documentation for `complete` alternative: https://ss64.com/osx/complete.html. I believe it's possible to fallback to `complete` but it should be done all over `/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone` (in 6 places which just ignore `compopt` if it's not present).

At this point, I'll report what I found just for the case you're curios (and for googlers). I think I know why I have the problem with process substitution: Bash doesn't support it in POSIX mode. In fact, 

```bash
21:07:03 [brandizi@brandizmac ~]$ set -o |grep posix
posix          	off
21:07:06 [brandizi@brandizmac ~]$ su -
Password:
-sh: /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone: line 266: syntax error near unexpected token `<'
-sh: /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/rclone: line 266: `            done < <(command rclone listremotes)'
21:07:14 [root@brandizmac ~]# set -o |grep posix
posix          	on
21:07:19 [root@brandizmac ~]# bash
21:07:22 [root@brandizmac ~]# set -o |grep posix
posix          	off
21:07:23 [root@brandizmac ~]# exit
21:07:29 [root@brandizmac ~]# logout
21:07:32 [brandizi@brandizmac ~]$
```
One solution might be `chsh -s /bin/bash`. But, I remembered about the `comopt` probelm too, so preferred to walk away from the rotten apple, by doing `brew install bash` (followed by a corresponding `chsh`). This fixed both the problems.

Last thing, given that you seem to have found a backward-compatible alternative for `comopt`, I wonder if you really need process substitution. It should be possible to rewrite the few fragments I've seen as: `command rclone listremotes | ...`
So where are we with this?  Shall we merge your patch @sgtpep ? Does it fix the problem?

@ncw My patch will eliminate the issue of `compopt` not being found on vanilla macOS `bash` that was reported by @marco-brandizi as:

> I get this when I try to auto-complete rclone:
> 
> ```shell
> 16:08:34 [brandizi@brandizmac luke]$ rclone ls -bash: compopt: command not found
> rres-onedrive:-bash: compopt: command not found
> ```
> 
> and then it works correctly.

So, I think, it worth being merged, although the issue is not fatal and doesn't break the autocomplete. Sorry for not providing it as a proper PR, didn't have time for that.

The main issue of this ticket is that autocomplete is defunct when bash is run under root on vanilla macOS `bash` because it happened to operate in `posix` mode for some reason. If I understand @marco-brandizi correctly, it's not a case for `brew`-installed `bash`.

We could debug this by placing `set -x` somewhere on top of bash init files to understand where `set -o posix` happens which enables posix mode for root. Or, we could just disable the whole autocomplete script if `posix` option is set (I could provide a patch for that, if needed.)
